title: Does Mentoring Help Students Belong?
summary: Boss: a whole two-group study from an SPSS file: import, score a scale with reverse-worded items, describe, check assumptions, test, plot and write it up in APA style.

steps.title: Import
steps.summary: Read the .sav file into `study`, with `condition` and `first_gen` as factors.

steps.title: Score
steps.summary: Reverse b2 and b4, average the five items into `belonging` (at least four answered), keep scored students in `analysed`, and find Cronbach's α.

steps.title: Describe
steps.summary: `group_stats`: n, M and SD of belonging per condition.

steps.title: Assumptions
steps.summary: Levene's test (SPSS-style) in `levene`; Shapiro–Wilk per group in `normality`.

steps.title: Test
steps.summary: Welch's t-test in `welch` and Cohen's d in `d`.

steps.title: Plot
steps.summary: `fig`: belonging by condition as a boxplot, with readable axis labels.

steps.title: Write it up
steps.summary: Your `decision` at α = .05 and the APA sentence in `write_up`.

hints: Import: `read_sav("belonging_study.sav") |> mutate(condition = as_factor(condition), first_gen = as_factor(first_gen))`. The 9s ("No answer") are already NA, because SPSS declared them missing.

Score: `mutate(across(b1:b5, zap_labels), b2 = 6 - b2, b4 = 6 - b4, answered = rowSums(!is.na(pick(b1:b5))), belonging = if_else(answered >= 4, rowMeans(pick(b1:b5), na.rm = TRUE), NA))`. Then `psych::alpha(select(analysed, b1:b5))$total$raw_alpha`.

Assumptions: `leveneTest(belonging ~ condition, data = analysed, center = mean)`; `normality` is `group_by(condition) |> summarise(W = shapiro.test(belonging)$statistic, p = shapiro.test(belonging)$p.value)`.
